item.title: Fetterman says he doesn't have a reason to leave Democratic Party
item.description: Over the weekend Major Garrett interviewed Sen. John Fetterman about his plans for 2028, whether he'd ever leave the Democratic Party, the war in Iran and more.

item.title: Iran says it's up to Trump to choose between war and diplomacy
item.description: As the war with Iran hits the seven-month mark, President Trump confirmed that American and Iranian negotiators exchanged messages through mediators on Monday.

item.title: Where things stand on talks as Trump rejects 7-day peace plan from Iran
item.description: A U.S. senior official tells CBS News that U.S.-Iran talks are making progress, but an Iranian diplomatic source says the talks aren't going well at all. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports from the White House and Ravi Agrawal, editor-in-chief for Foreign Policy, joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: Trump to meet with AI leaders about safety as Bill Gates lays out stark warning
item.description: President Trump is set to meet with AI leaders about the technology's safety on Tuesday after Bill Gates over the weekend laid out a stark warning about artificial intelligence's potential dangers. CBS News' Nancy Cordes reports.

item.title: How Iran and recent Supreme Court decisions will impact the 2026 midterms
item.description: The Supreme Court has ruled on several changes to voting proposed by the Trump administration. Most recently, it ruled that the Trump administration could use a controversial database to review state voter rolls for potential non-citizens. David Becker, executive director and founder of the Center for Election Innovation and Research, joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Peperoncini product recalled after "pest contaminant" found in jar
item.description: California food manufacturer said it is investigating after a consumer posted a video showing a rodent in a jar of the company's peperoncinis.

item.title: Hurricane Polo approaches Mexico, threatens Southwest U.S. with flooding
item.description: Hurricane Polo could bring "life-threatening winds and flash floods" to Mexico's Baja California Sur and nearby Sonora and then heavy rain and flooding to parts of the U.S.

item.title: Top AI companies probing tens of thousands of AI security incidents, Axios reports
item.description: Axios reports that OpenAI, Anthropic and security researchers are investigating tens of thousands of cases where AI models showed troublesome behavior like bypassing guardrails, creating message boards and even hacking websites. New York Times technology correspondent Mike Isaac joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Holiday airfares soar to 10-year high. Here's how to save on flights.
item.description: Airfares for round-trip U.S. flights have jumped 31% compared to the same period last year, and tickets are likely to get pricier, according to a new analysis.

item.title: Closing arguments to start in trial of former "American Idol" contestant accused of killing wife
item.description: Closing arguments are set to begin Tuesday in the trial of former "American Idol" contestant Caleb Flynn, who's accused of killing his wife. CBS News' Ian Lee has more.

item.title: Trump announces plans for largest steel plant in U.S. history to be built in Iowa
item.description: President Trump on Monday announced that the company Mesabi Metallics will build a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa over the coming years.

item.title: New York Times exec dies in California shooting; elderly in-laws accused of murder
item.description: An elderly couple in the San Francisco Bay Area is suspected of shooting and killing their son-in-law in the parking lot of a community park over the weekend.

item.title: Gas prices could soar if the U.S. bans diesel exports, economists say
item.description: President Trump said he is "very seriously" considering a ban on diesel exports. But such a move could drive U.S. gas prices sharply higher, analysts said.

item.title: Broadview 6 prosecutor retires under protest, blames U.S. attorney
item.description: Sheri Mecklenburg resigned from the Department of Justice this week, penning a scathing letter in which she said U.S. Attorney Andrew Boutros "personally directed" the Broadview 6 prosecution that she says ended her career.

item.title: Trump administration rolls back Biden-era fuel economy standards
item.description: Regulators estimate the new rule will result in an average of 34.9 miles per gallon by model year 2031, down from an earlier projection of 50.4 mpg.

item.title: Details emerge in case of former Cornell student alleging rape by frat members
item.description: A woman, identified only as Jane Doe, alleges she was gang-raped by seven fraternity members in 2024 and accuses Cornell University of failing to protect her.

item.title: Alito recuses himself from major case on climate change and fossil fuels
item.description: The Supreme Court will soon hear arguments in the major climate change lawsuit between two energy companies and the city and county of Boulder, Colorado.

item.title: Inside the significance of SpaceX's first orbital flight of Super Heavy-Starship
item.description: SpaceX on Monday successfully launched its Super Heavy-Starship on its first flight to orbit. Kristin Fisher, founder and executive producer of Endless Void Studios, joined CBS News to discuss what this means for space exploration moving forward.

item.title: OpenAI agents used aggressive techniques to access U.N. website, Wall Street Journal reports
item.description: The Wall Street Journal reports that OpenAI used aggressive techniques to access the United Nations' website in June. Wall Street Journal reporter Robert McMillian joins CBS News to discuss.

item.title: Pope Leo draws massive crowds in France. Is Catholicism making a comeback?
item.description: Large crowds in Paris and other parts of France offered a striking welcome for Pope Leo in one of Europe's most secular countries.

item.title: Nor'easter continuing to lash East Coast with flood alerts still in effect
item.description: The nor'easter that swamped much of the Eastern Seaboard over the weekend is still dropping rain as it slowly moves up the coast. CBS News' Tom Hanson and Jessica Burch have more.

item.title: Trump had private dinner with Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei
item.description: The dinner comes as Amodei has warned about the "exponential growth" of AI, and has called for safeguards on the industry, which President Trump has rejected.

item.title: Top FBI official Andrew Bailey resigns
item.description: Bailey was originally brought in to help ease tensions between former Attorney General Pam Bondi and former FBI Deputy Director Dan Bongino.

item.title: SpaceX launches Starship on giant rocket's first flight to orbit
item.description: The Super Heavy-Starship rocket's 14th test flight, the first boosting the upper stage to orbit, marked a major milestone for both SpaceX and NASA.

item.title: How Trump is taking on AI as concerns about rogue agents explode
item.description: President Trump is meeting with the heads of AI giants as the global concern about rogue models lingers. This comes as more details emerge about OpenAI agents apparently scanning the United Nations website thousands of times. CBS News' Weijia Jiang reports, and The Verge's Terrence O'Brien joins with more on his reporting.

item.title: BASE jumper dies after falling from 700-foot Utah cliff
item.description: A 27-year-old BASE jumper died on Sunday, after falling about 700 feet from a cliff in Utah, authorities said.

item.title: Nvidia announces security system to stop AI agents from going rogue
item.description: Nvidia said more than 100 organizations are using the platform, which it says could have stopped the Hugging Face hack by OpenAI agents.

item.title: Food safety becomes election issue as major outbreaks, recalls cause concern
item.description: Recent outbreaks of foodborne illness and high-profile recalls have made food safety a concern of voters.

item.title: Georgia park mass shooting wounds 11 teens at birthday party
item.description: The wounded victims were identified as four 18-year-old men, five 17-year-old boys and two 18-year-old women, according to the sheriff's office.

item.title: Wastin' Away Again in Margaritaville… With No Estate Plan?! | Money Moves with Jill Schlesinger
item.description: Why are Jill and Mark doing a deep dive on Margaritaville? Well, three years have passed since Jimmy Buffett died, and his family is still fighting over a $275 million estate. In today's episode, Jill and Mark explain why estate planning is essential and why you don't need to be rich to need a trust. Plus, how did caller Sam accumulate $370,000 by age 30 on a $95,000 salary?!
